      <content name="altTitle">&lt;span class="qt1"&gt;Leg&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class="qt2"&gt;Cramps&lt;/span&gt;</content>
      <content name="FullSummary">What are &lt;span class="qt3"&gt;muscle &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class="qt2"&gt;&lt;span class="qt3"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;?&lt;p&gt;&lt;span class="qt3"&gt;Muscle &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class="qt2"&gt;&lt;span class="qt3"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; are sudden, involuntary contractions or spasms in one or more of your muscles. They are very common and often occur after exercise. Some people get &lt;span class="qt3"&gt;muscle &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class="qt2"&gt;&lt;span class="qt3"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;, especially &lt;span class="qt1"&gt;leg&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class="qt2"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;, at &lt;span class="qt0"&gt;night&lt;/span&gt;. They can be painful, and they may last a few seconds to several minutes.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;You can have a &lt;span class="qt2"&gt;cramp&lt;/span&gt; in any muscle, but they happen most often in the:&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Thighs&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Feet&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Hands&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Arms&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Abdomen&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Area along your ribcage&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;What causes &lt;span class="qt3"&gt;muscle &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class="qt2"&gt;&lt;span class="qt3"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;?&lt;p&gt;Causes of &lt;span class="qt3"&gt;muscle &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class="qt2"&gt;&lt;span class="qt3"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; include:&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Straining or overusing a muscle. This is the most common cause.&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Compression of your nerves, from problems such as a spinal cord injury or a pinched nerve in the neck or back&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Dehydration&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Low levels of electrolytes such as magnesium, potassium, or calcium&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Not enough blood getting to your muscles&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Pregnancy&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Certain medicines&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Getting dialysis&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;p&gt;Sometimes the cause of &lt;span class="qt3"&gt;muscle &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class="qt2"&gt;&lt;span class="qt3"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; is unknown.&lt;/p&gt;Who is at risk for &lt;span class="qt3"&gt;muscle &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class="qt2"&gt;&lt;span class="qt3"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;?&lt;p&gt;Anyone can get &lt;span class="qt3"&gt;muscle &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class="qt2"&gt;&lt;span class="qt3"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;, but they are more common in some people:&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;span class="qt4"&gt;Older&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class="qt5"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;adults&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;People who are overweight&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Athletes&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Pregnant women&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;People with certain medical conditions, such as thyroid and nerve disorders&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;When do I need to see a health care provider for &lt;span class="qt3"&gt;muscle &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class="qt2"&gt;&lt;span class="qt3"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;?&lt;p&gt;&lt;span class="qt3"&gt;Muscle &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class="qt2"&gt;&lt;span class="qt3"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; are usually harmless, and they go away after a few minutes. But you should contact your health care provider if the &lt;span class="qt2"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;:&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Are severe&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Happen frequently&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Don't get better with stretching and drinking enough fluids&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Last a long time&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Are accompanied by swelling, redness, or a feeling of warmth&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Are accompanied by muscle weakness&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;What are the treatments for &lt;span class="qt3"&gt;muscle &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class="qt2"&gt;&lt;span class="qt3"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;?&lt;p&gt;You usually don't need treatment for &lt;span class="qt3"&gt;muscle &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class="qt2"&gt;&lt;span class="qt3"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;. You may be able to find some relief from &lt;span class="qt2"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt; by:&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Stretching or gently massaging the muscle&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Applying heat when the muscle is tight and ice when the muscle is sore&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Getting more fluids if you are dehydrated&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;p&gt;If another medical problem is causing the &lt;span class="qt2"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;, treating that problem will likely help. There are medicines that providers sometimes prescribe to prevent &lt;span class="qt2"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;, but they are not always effective and may cause side effects. Talk to your provider about the risks and benefits of medicines.&lt;/p&gt;Can &lt;span class="qt3"&gt;muscle &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class="qt2"&gt;&lt;span class="qt3"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; be prevented?&lt;p&gt;To prevent &lt;span class="qt3"&gt;muscle &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class="qt2"&gt;&lt;span class="qt3"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;, you can:&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Stretch your muscles, especially before exercising. If you often get &lt;span class="qt1"&gt;leg&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class="qt2"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt; at &lt;span class="qt0"&gt;night&lt;/span&gt;, stretch your &lt;span class="qt1"&gt;leg&lt;/span&gt; muscles before bed.&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Drink plenty of liquids. If you do intense exercise or exercise in the heat, sports drinks can help you replace electrolytes.&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;</content>
